verdicts.note: Elio (transcript, on Yandel): 'the section on Robert and the Rebellion is very limited and very particular on what it shows. He's someone who's intensely aware ... when he's writing about very powerful people like Tywin Lannister, he needs to be careful.' Quote verbatim; every limb (limited/particular section, Yandel's awareness, Tywin) on the page. Page says 'Robert and the Rebellion'.

verdicts.trueWording: A lot of books we came up with
verdicts.note: Elio: 'We would add ... when you hear the name of a new maester, and a book by a new maester that you haven't heard about before. A lot of books we came up with. That was the one area where George was fine with us having a little fun and making little references'. Quote verbatim; invented maesters and the 'one area George was fine with us having fun' limb both present.

Elio: 'My favorites passages from George are very poetic passages, like the first Aero Hotah chapter and his prose is gorgeous'. Quote verbatim; both limbs present. The transcript spells the name 'Aero Hotah'.

verdicts.trueWording: George is fantastic in creating atmosphere and theme
verdicts.note: Elio on Guy Gavriel Kay: 'He writes very beautifully, in a way distinctly from George. George is fantastic in creating atmosphere and theme and his characters in greater detail, but Kay is almost poetic in how he writes'. Quote verbatim; all three limbs (Martin/atmosphere+theme, Kay/almost poetic, distinctly different) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: we started cutting the material down to fit into this book
verdicts.note: Linda: 'he wrote the material really originally for TWOIAF and it had sort of ballooned in size and became too big, and we started cutting the material down to fit into this book, so when the time came for him to put the unedited material into Fire and Blood...'. Quote verbatim; both limbs present, and the speaker is Antonsson as the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: Antonsson: versioning control was definitely a bit of a problem
verdicts.note: The quoted sentence is verbatim on the page but it is Linda Antonsson speaking, not Garcia: 'Linda: ... George would often work from his original files, which weren't necessarily the files that had then gone back to us and through Anne's editing. So, the all versioning control was definitely a bit of a problem'. Garcia separately supports the WordStar limb elsewhere on the page ('George wouldn't refer to those when he looked back to his original WordStar files where we didn't have any comments'), and 'Anne, the editor' is Anne Groell (named in full in the page's correction note). Substance of the claim is on the page; only the speaker attribution in the claim sentence fails. Note also that Antonsson's own sentence says 'his original files', not 'WordStar files'.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the claim's attribution to Garcia - the versioning-control sentence is spoken by Antonsson

verdicts.trueWording: try and keep it consistent between the two books
verdicts.note: Linda: 'we helped Anne and so on to go over it and try and keep it consistent between the two books' (the two books being Fire and Blood and The World of Ice and Fire). Quote verbatim; speaker is Antonsson as claimed; 'Anne' is Anne Groell, named in full on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: mainly because we had to shorten a few elements in the book
verdicts.note: Groell, first-page Q&A on knowing the ending: 'I do know a few things from AWOW, but mainly because we had to shorten a few elements in the book as it was already getting too long'. Quote fragment verbatim; both limbs (elements shortened, book already too long) present. 'AWOW' is her shorthand for The World of Ice and Fire, which she names in full one answer earlier ('while editing THE WORLD OF ICE AND FIRE').

verdicts.trueWording: he had to reveal a few secrets so I could help him redirect parts of the plot
verdicts.note: Groell: '...and he had to reveal a few secrets so I could help him redirect parts of the plot a bit.' Quote verbatim. The book limb rests on the same sentence, whose subject is the AWOW/World of Ice and Fire editing ('we had to shorten a few elements in the book'); the page does not re-name the book at the word 'plot'.

Groell, first answer: 'I begin to wonder-though 7 is what we currently have under contract... He predicted four books. I said Seven Books for Seven Kingdoms. Then he said five books. I said Seven Books for Seven Kingdoms. Then he went to six. I said... Well, you get it.' Quote verbatim; both limbs (seven under contract, the repeated answer to each revised estimate) present.

verdicts.trueWording: internal consistency is to my mind a good objective yardstick
verdicts.note: Speech, in the disclaimers before the three rules: 'To name one obvious one, internal consistency is to my mind a good objective yardstick by which to judge a piece of fiction.' Quote verbatim; the claim reproduces the whole sentence's sense.

verdicts.trueWording: lives events as the viewpoint character lives them
verdicts.note: Speech: 'Ideally a reader is absorbed into a narratives and lives events as the viewpoint character lives them, learns things as he learns them, and so on.' Quote verbatim; all three limbs present ('narratives' is a typo in the page text).

verdicts.trueWording: I organize things - events and information and the like
verdicts.note: Speech: 'Look, when I sit down and write a story, I'm trying to give my reader a vicarious experience. I organize things - events and information and the like - as carefully as I can'. Quote verbatim (em dashes match); both limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: We read fiction to find out what happens
verdicts.note: Speech, immediately after the Garp/Jillsy Sloper quotation: 'We eat to fuel our bodies, We read fiction to find out what happens.' Quote verbatim; the section placement in the claim's page field is correct.

verdicts.trueWording: it needs to be logical and consistent and integral
verdicts.note: Speech, in the passage on the sacrosanct protected ending: 'The ending of a piece of fiction should grow out of what has gone before; it needs to be logical and consistent and integral to the rest of the story.' Quote verbatim; both limbs present.
